bullets.title: MU: Blowout Q3 beat drives AI memory bull case; memory tight through 2027
bullets.body: Micron reported fiscal 3Q26 revenue of $41.5B with 81% operating margins, signing 16 Strategic Customer Agreements guaranteeing $100B+ in minimum revenue with price floors above prior cycle peaks. AI server memory demand exceeded $25B in the quarter; cumulative HBM4 revenue surpassed $1B. Memory supply expected to remain tight through 2027 with only gradual improvement in 2028, consistent read-across for semis equipment.

bullets.title: Semis broadly selling off pre-market; MU +5% but sector -3-5%
bullets.body: Despite MU's beat, broader semiconductor names are down 3-5% pre-market: AAOI -5.1%, MU +5.1% (on earnings), SNDK -5.1%, WDC -4.4%, MRVL -3.9%, LITE -3.8%, AMD -3.3%, INTC -3.0%. Pressure stems from Samsung/SK Hynix announcing massive new AI investment (~$648B Samsung plan), raising supply overhang fears, plus OpenAI IPO delay and memory cost inflation hitting hardware margins.

bullets.title: AAPL: 15-25% Mac/iPad price hikes signal memory cost crunch; iPhone 18 cycle next
bullets.body: Apple raised Mac, iPad, and accessories prices 15-25% ($30-$500 absolute), earlier and larger than most analysts expected, signaling low-cost DRAM/NAND inventory is depleted. JPM's prior mid-single-digit iPhone price increase estimate now looks too conservative; MS had modeled 5-10%. iPhone prices not raised yet — likely held for the September iPhone 18 launch with foldable. JPM specialist call argues memory cost anxiety is overpriced given product price hikes support record margins and carrier/installment financing provides demand inelasticity.

bullets.title: MSFT: Italian antitrust investigation into M365 price hike; software +1.3% pre-market
bullets.body: Italy's AGCM launched a formal investigation into Microsoft over the Microsoft 365/Copilot price increase, citing failure to clearly disclose AI service integration and default enrollment in higher-priced tiers. Despite headline risk, MSFT trades +1.3% pre-market, outperforming the broader tech selloff alongside other software names (NOW +1.5%, ADBE +1.2%, PLTR +1.7%). Citi US Equity Strategy cut Information Technology from OW to Market Weight.

bullets.title: Citi cuts Tech/Semis/Hardware to Market Weight on Mag 7 weakness and margin pressure
bullets.body: Citi's US Equity Strategy downgraded Information Technology, Semis, and Hardware from Overweight to Market Weight, citing Mag 7 down 7% YTD, four structural headwinds (funding concerns, company-specific issues, competition, technicals breaking 200DMA), and memory price inflation squeezing hardware margins. Software & Services upgraded to Market Weight. Mag 7 constituents AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, NVDA, AVGO all flagged with specific issues.

bullets.title: AMZN: JPM initiates on Focus List with $330 PT; advertising an AI beneficiary
bullets.body: JPM raises AMZN to Overweight with $330 PT (32x 2027E EPS of $10.38), placing it on the Analyst Focus List. AMZN advertising projected at ~$83B revenue in 2026 (+21% FXN YoY) at ~46% operating margins (~$38B OI), the third-largest digital ad platform globally. AI/ML improving ad ranking/ROAS; agentic commerce (Alexa+ Agentic Ads) seen as an incremental TAM expander. Prime Day saw mixed results with 5.3% YoY spending growth to $8.3B but average order down 18% to $47.

bullets.title: DKNG: PM volumes +265% YoY annualized on World Cup; proprietary exchange launch +1.6%
bullets.body: DraftKings prediction market volumes annualized at $11.3B with $3.4B consumer volumes in the week ended 6/21, up +265% and +160% annualized from May levels, driven by World Cup Group Stage activity. NY OSB data for the same week shows DraftKings +1% GGR YoY, maintaining ~33% share, though 2QTD GGR tracks -21% YoY amid hold rate compression. Virtual group meeting with IR scheduled June 29.

bullets.title: PENN: Goldman initiates Buy at $26 PT; JPM bullish after Hollywood Aurora tour
bullets.body: Goldman initiates PENN at Buy with $26 PT (23% upside from $21.09), citing regional gaming inflection as supply headwinds fade, a $1B development pipeline, Interactive nearing profitability, and recurring FCF/share >$4 by 2028. JPM toured the newly opened Hollywood Aurora (June 24, $360M, 1,000 slots, 226 hotel rooms) and sees faster margin ramp via Joliet learnings; Joliet GGR tracking +70% YoY. PENN targeting 15% cash-on-cash returns across four development projects.

bullets.title: RRR: Goldman initiates Buy at $72 PT as 2027 earnings inflection story
bullets.body: Goldman initiates Red Rock Resorts at Buy with $72 PT (13% upside from $63.57), calling it a durable compounder with 2027 as the key earnings inflection year. RRR benefits from lapping 2026 disruption headwinds, harvesting growth from five recent projects, and is a pure-play on the attractive Las Vegas Locals market with land bank optionality.

bullets.title: APP: Down ~4% on boutique report citing US gaming slowdown
bullets.body: APP fell ~4% pre-market following a boutique sell-side report citing a US gaming market slowdown, mixed eCommerce feedback, and META not yet competing for non-IDFA traffic. JPM notes channel tone has modestly improved since February on stable eCommerce datapoints and continued mobile gaming strength, partially offsetting the bearish read.

bullets.title: QCOM: DZ Bank upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $265 from $195 (29% upside)
bullets.body: DZ Bank upgraded Qualcomm to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $265 from $195, implying 29% upside from $204.90. The FactSet consensus target stands at $221.93. No specific catalyst cited beyond the upgrade itself.

bullets.title: NVDA/GOOGL/TSLA: Underperforming pre-market as Mag 7 rotation accelerates
bullets.body: JPM's morning briefing notes NVDA, GOOGL, and TSLA underperforming pre-market as sector rotation intensifies away from Mag 7 into AI Memory and Data Centers. Goldman and BofA both frame Big Tech as the funding source for the rotation into semis and memory stocks. JPM maintains Tactically Bullish call but expects the 'everything rally' to fade into concentrated leadership.

bullets.title: LITE/CRDO: Optical beneficiaries flagged on ON/SYNA deal and CPO/OCS roadmap
bullets.body: Mizuho notes LITE positioned as a leading MEMS supplier in OCS ramp, and flags LITE and CRDO explicitly as optical roadmap beneficiaries alongside NVDA and AVGO. CPO deliveries could materialize in 2028/29E. The ON/SYNA deal expands edge AI and connectivity but the optical read-across to these names is the more direct signal.

bullets.title: NOW/ADBE/CRM/ORCL: CIO survey shows enterprise app budgets under pressure as AI infra dominates
bullets.body: A CIO survey shows IT budget growth at 3.9% for 2026/4.0% for 2027, but the dollars are flowing to AI infrastructure and security (security budgets +130bps to 4.4%). Enterprise application vendors are seeing net declines in CIO priority spend: MSFT, NOW, ORCL, CRM, ADBE all down. 62% of respondents have AI in meaningful production, up 20pts vs. 2H25, and 64% expect budget scrutiny to intensify.

bullets.title: INTU: Wolfe cuts PT to $350 from $400 (Outperform) on pricing concentration risk
bullets.body: Wolfe Research cut its Intuit price target to $350 from $400 while maintaining Outperform, citing QuickBooks platform price increases concentrated in higher tiers with early Bill Pay monetization seen as limited near-term upside driver. Separately, INTU announced a price increase flagged by Wolfe SaaS Daily. IGV has returned -15.7% YTD vs. S&P +10.1%.

bullets.title: NFLX: Wolfe Outperform at $107 PT; 19x forward P/E seen as entry point
bullets.body: Wolfe Research highlights Netflix at 19x forward P/E as an attractive entry relative to history, calling it one of few stocks that matches quality-growth-price criteria. Streaming survey (MS) shows AMZN Prime, NFLX, and YouTube with the strongest engagement and stickiness, with 90% of services seeing YoY engagement increases. House of Dragon Season 3 debuted with 21.5M viewers in three days.

bullets.title: ADBE: Acquires Topaz Labs; SaaS multiples compressing week-over-week
bullets.body: Adobe announced the acquisition of Topaz Labs (AI-powered image/video enhancement tools), adding to its AI creative stack. All-SaaS multiples are down 2.22% week-over-week; All-Security down 1.46%; All-Vertical down 2.30% per Wolfe's index.

bullets.title: BABA: Down 6.3% on day, -20% YTD amid broad China tech selloff
bullets.body: Alibaba (BABA US/9988.HK) fell 6.3% on the day and is -20% YTD as China internet stocks broadly sold off. GS Spec Sales notes Alibaba -33% YTD. On a more positive note, Alimama's AI tool WanXiang was invoked 3B+ times during the 618 shopping festival with 20% ROI improvement for merchants.

bullets.title: VZ/T: Starlink mobile launch for US consumers flagged as competitive threat
bullets.body: SpaceX is planning to launch a new Starlink mobile service for US consumers per the FT, which could represent a longer-term competitive threat to wireless carriers. T and VZ were largely unchanged pre-market following the news, suggesting market views near-term impact as limited.

bullets.title: SHOP: Campaigns monetization emerging as long-term growth driver per UBS
bullets.body: UBS flagged Shopify Campaigns/lead generation via the Shop app as a potentially meaningful long-term growth driver, enabling merchants to acquire customers at attributable CAC. Stripe Link users exceed 300M+ vs. PayPal's 439M TTM active accounts for context on addressable user base. No rating change or PT move disclosed in this note.
